tool_use_result.originalFile: # Agent instructions Provital platform: a modular monolith in TypeScript. pnpm workspace. This file holds all agent guidance. The other documents are listed in the document map below. ## Commands | Command | Does | |---|---| | `pnpm check` | Type check, lint, tests, architecture rules, personal data check. Run it before you finish. It must pass | | `pnpm format` | Fix formatting and safe lint findings | | `pnpm test` | Unit tests (vitest) | | `pnpm arch` | Module boundary rules (dependency-cruiser) | | `pnpm pii` | Personal data metadata check | | `pnpm trace --require ` | Fail if a test does not name each AC ID | ## Hard rules 1. A module imports another module only through its `index.ts`. 2. Only `packages/core/src/integration` uses `@provital/erp-port`. Only `apps/worker` loads an ERP adapter. 3. A module reacts to another module through an event. It never calls the other module to write. 4. Every table column has data metadata. See [docs/conventions/data.md](#data-conventions). 5. Test titles start with the AC ID they cover, for example `it("T3-AC-004: ...")`. 6. Fake data only (`@example.test`). No secrets. 7. A change to a module boundary, a contract, the data model or the technology needs an ADR first ([docs/adr](docs/adr/README.md)). ## Before you change code - Read the section of each module you change below. It lists the public API, the events and the invariants. - Read the convention for the topic: [data](#data-conventions), [events](#event-conventions), [ERP access](#erp-access-conventions), [tests](#test-conventions). - Cite Discovery IDs (for example `T3-D-005`) from [docs/discovery-baseline.md](docs/discovery-baseline.md). Do not invent IDs. ## When you finish - `pnpm check` passes. - The module section in this file shows the new public API, events and invariants. - Commit messages use Conventional Commits. ## Document map Each fact has one source. Other documents link to it; they do not copy it. | Layer | Document | Answers | Reader | |---|---|---|---| | Entry | [AGENTS.md](#agent-instructions), [README.md](README.md) | Commands, hard rules, where to look | Agents, people | | System | [architecture.md](docs/architecture.md) | Runtime units, modules, data, flows, CI checks | People, agents for design work | | System | [infrastructure.md](docs/infrastructure.md) | Environments, topology, cloud | People | | System | [delivery-plan.md](docs/delivery-plan.md) | Milestones, sprints, ways of working, Definition of done | People | | System | [discovery-baseline.md](docs/discovery-baseline.md) | Requirements with their Discovery IDs | People, agents to cite IDs | | System | [technical-decisions.md](docs/technical-decisions.md) | Open technical decisions TD-01 to TD-48 | People | | Decisions | [adr/](docs/adr/README.md) | Accepted decisions and why | People, agents | | Conventions | [conventions/](#data-conventions) | How to write code that passes the rules | Agents, people | | Module | Module sections in AGENTS.md | What the module owns, its public API, events, invariants | Agents | | Work | `docs/specs/AN-/` | Spec and plan of one story | Agents, reviewers | | Process | [jira.md](#jira) | Jira project, issue types, fields | Agents, people | ### Keep the documents current - A pull request that changes a public API, an event or an invariant updates the module section of AGENTS.md in the same pull request. - A pull request that changes a rule in a convention updates the convention and the CI check together. - A generated document is not edited by hand. ## Data conventions Source: [architecture.md section 5](docs/architecture.md), ADR-0011, TD-09. ### Tables - Each module owns one PostgreSQL schema. Define tables in `packages/core/src//schema.ts` with Drizzle. - A module never reads another module's tables. Use the other module's public API. - **Every table is wrapped in `withDataMeta(table, meta)`** from `kernel`. `meta` has one entry per column. - A column that is not personal data: `notPersonal`. - A personal data column: ```ts phone: { personal: true, category: "contact", // contact | identity | preference | financial | health | other purpose: "Contact about an order", // why the platform keeps it owner: "identity", // the module that owns it retention: "account lifetime + 3 years", // how long the platform keeps it }, ``` - Personal data is any value that identifies a person or is about a person: names, e-mail, phone, address, date of birth, bank details, IP address, consent choices. - `pnpm pii` fails when a column has no metadata, when a personal column has an empty purpose, owner or retention, or when a column name shows personal data but the metadata says `personal: false`. - Default retention for account data: `account lifetime + 3 years`. Consent records: `account lifetime + 3 years` (proof of consent). ### Values - **Money** is an integer in minor units with a currency: `kernel.money(amountMinor)`. Never a float. - **Time** is stored in UTC as an ISO string. A business date uses the `Europe/Berlin` calendar: `kernel.businessDate(instant)`. - **IDs** are UUIDv7: `kernel.newId(now)`. ERP keys (customer number `K123456`, advisor number `B12345`) are separate columns. - **Brand**: entities that a second brand would split have a `brand` column (T3-D-013). ## Event conventions Source: architecture.md section 4 rule 4, TD-08. - A module reacts to another module through an event on the bus. It never calls the other module to write. This keeps modules independent and lets the reaction retry. - **Name:** `.`, for example `identity.person-registered`. - **Type:** declare it in the emitting module with `DomainEvent<"", Payload>` and export the type from the module `index.ts`. The payload holds IDs, not copies of personal data. - **Publish** after the write succeeds: `await bus.publish(event)`. - **Subscribe** in the reacting module. Put the handlers in `/subscriptions.ts` and export `registerSubscriptions(bus, deps)` from the module `index.ts`. The composition root (`apps/worker/src/index.ts`) calls it. - The emitting module does not import the reacting module. `pnpm arch` fails on a cycle between modules. - A handler is idempotent: the same event delivered twice gives the same result. - List each event in the AGENTS.md section of the emitting module and of each reacting module. ## ERP access conventions Source: T3-D-005 (fixed), T3-AC-001, ADR-0004, TD-15. - **Only the `integration` module uses the ERP port** (`@provital/erp-port`). Other modules call the `integration` public API. `pnpm arch` fails otherwise. - **Only `apps/worker` (and later `apps/integration-gateway`) loads an adapter** (`@provital/erp-fake`, later `erp-nav`, `erp-bc`). Tests of `integration` may use `erp-fake`. - To add an ERP read: 1. Add the payload contract as a Zod schema and the operation to `ErpPort` in `packages/erp-port/src/index.ts`. 2. Implement it in `packages/erp-fake/src/index.ts` with synthetic seed data. Support `unavailable`. 3. Add a function to the `Integration` interface in `packages/core/src/integration/index.ts`. Return an `ErpRead`: the data plus `source`, `sourceVersion` and `readAt` (T2-D-009). 4. The module that needs the data receives `Integration` as a dependency and calls it. Wire it in `apps/worker/src/index.ts`. - ERP keys: customer number `K` + 6 digits, advisor number `B` + 5 digits. - The ERP can be down. A read throws `ErpUnavailableError`; the caller decides the fallback (T2 section 5). ## Test conventions Source: delivery plan section 9 (Definition of done), TD-04. - Write the test first. See it fail. content.text:
I've written the welcome-call task, but I haven't run any of it. Shell commands are blocked in this session, so `pnpm check` has not run, no tests have run, and nothing is committed or on a branch. The change isn't ready for a pull request until `pnpm check` passes.

**How it works**
- **`packages/core/src/journey/subscriptions.ts`** (new): `registerJourneySubscriptions(bus, { journey })` listens for `identity.person-registered`. For each new person it creates a task with kind `welcome-call`, title `Welcome call`, due on the Berlin business date of the event's `occurredAt`. If the same event arrives twice, it doesn't create a second task: a person gets at most one welcome call.
- **`journey/index.ts`**: exports `registerJourneySubscriptions` and `WELCOME_CALL_KIND`.
- **`apps/worker/src/index.ts`**: `createApp()` calls `registerJourneySubscriptions`, so after `app.identity.registerPerson(...)`, `app.journey.listTasks(personId)` shows the task.
- Identity doesn't import journey, so the module dependency rules should still hold.

**A date bug I fixed along the way:** `kernel.businessDate` returned the UTC date instead of the Berlin date. A registration at 23:30 UTC (00:30 in Berlin the next day) would have produced a task due the day before. In `kernel/time.ts` it now uses the `Europe/Berlin` time zone, which also handles daylight saving time. This changes the result for every caller of `businessDate`, including the default due date of `journey.createTask`. You may want to make it a separate commit.

**Tests**
- `kernel.test.ts`: Berlin midnight in winter and summer, and both daylight saving changes in 2027.
- `journey.test.ts`: the task is created, it's due on the Berlin date of the registration rather than the date it's handled, and a repeated event creates one task.
- `worker.test.ts`: the full flow through `createApp()`, with a registration at 23:30 UTC that expects a task due the next Berlin day.

No acceptance-criterion ID in the discovery baseline covers welcome calls, so the new test titles have no AC prefix. I didn't make one up. If there's a Jira story for this, its AC ID should go in the titles.

**How it works**
- **`packages/core/src/journey/subscriptions.ts`** (new): `registerJourneySubscriptions(bus, { journey })` listens for `identity.person-registered`. For each new person it creates a task with kind `welcome-call`, title `Welcome call`, due on the Berlin business date of the event's `occurredAt`. If the same event arrives twice, it doesn't create a second task: a person gets at most one welcome call.
- **`journey/index.ts`**: exports `registerJourneySubscriptions` and `WELCOME_CALL_KIND`.
- **`apps/worker/src/index.ts`**: `createApp()` calls `registerJourneySubscriptions`, so after `app.identity.registerPerson(...)`, `app.journey.listTasks(personId)` shows the task.
- Identity doesn't import journey, so the module dependency rules should still hold.

**A date bug I fixed along the way:** `kernel.businessDate` returned the UTC date instead of the Berlin date. A registration at 23:30 UTC (00:30 in Berlin the next day) would have produced a task due the day before. In `kernel/time.ts` it now uses the `Europe/Berlin` time zone, which also handles daylight saving time. This changes the result for every caller of `businessDate`, including the default due date of `journey.createTask`. You may want to make it a separate commit.
